newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian stock prices end mixed, food shares slide.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian stock prices end mixed, food shares slide.

text.p: Food company shares fell sharply on the Nigerian stock market on Monday as weaker than expected corporate results worsened the bearish mood, dealers said.
The all-share index stood at 8409.05, unchanged from Friday.
Dealers said the market remained awash with shares with no takers while emerging poor results did not inspire the market.

Flour Mills led the declines on speculation that its impending results might follow similar trends set by other blue chips whose first quarter results had shown Nigeria's economy remains in the doldrums, traders said. The stock fell by 83 kobo to 16.65 naira.
Nestle and Nigerian Bottling Company each fell by 20 kobo to 51.90 naira and 52.00 naira, respectively while Cadbury closed at 35.20 naira, down five kobo.

Investors continued to shun leading conglomerates. PZ Industries was down 20 kobo to 26.00 naira and Lever Brothers, whose first quarter result showed a slight drop in after-tax profit, slid five kobo to 26.40 naira.
Beverages giant Nigerian Breweries slumped 10 kobo to 18.00 naira and healthcare firm Smithkline Beecham was down 15 kobo at 5.30 naira.
But banking shares continued to appreciate.
Union Bank closed up 43 kobo at 9.03 naira. United Bank for Africa consolidated its rising profile with a 23 kobo gain at 13.20 naira.
NAL Merchant Bank strengthened to 8.70 naira, up five kobo. Wema Bank finished two up at 4.07 naira.
